newsitem.title: USA: US T-bond futures end day up,but down for the week.
newsitem.headline: US T-bond futures end day up,but down for the week.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed the day higher, with March T-bonds rebounding from a key technical support area, but ending down 19/32 points on the week.
March T-bonds continued to find upside momentum after holding losses above the 112-08/32 to 112-09/32 area earlier in the session.

Leveraged and nonleveraged accounts were active buyers after March demonstrated its resiliency above 112-08/32, a one-month low set last Friday in after-hours trade. The contract would have retraced 38 percent of its three-month upmove at the 112-09/32 level, analysts said.
The sentiment turned bullish in the short term, pushing March to 113-14/32. Eurodollar traders lifted June to 94.40, as Eurodollars also became oversold in the near term.
James Bianco, director of research at Arbor Trading Group Inc, was not surprised at March bonds' ability to contain losses at 112-08/32, near a break-out level from October 29.
Bianco said speculators became heavy buyers at that level, accounting for the surge in open interest from late October.
"It was a technical even when we broke from that level. Since then, open interest has increased 100,000, and the buying was from speculators," Bianco said.
Open interest rose to its highest level of the year on Wednesday. Total bond futures open interest increased more than 14,000 contracts to about 501,000 contracts.

Bianco said the bond futures market has a difficult time sustaining open interest above 500,000, especially as speculators have already established long positions. The last time bond futures open interest totaled more than 500,000 was in August 1996 when prices set an intermediate-term top.
"How many speculators do we have left?" he asked. "For the market to go higher from here we would need real investors."
He said investors, looking for long-term value, continue to put their money into the stock market.
As a result, March bonds will inevitably break below the 112-08/32 area. Many technical analysts are forecasting a decline to the 111-16/32 and 111-00 area.
However, that decline may be postponed until after the holidays as the market, as of next week, will enter a seasonal period of unpredictability, Bianco said.
"You can almost throw out any indicator from December 15 to the first week of January," he said.

At the end of pit trade, March bonds were 24/32 higher at 113-08/32, 10-year notes were up 15/32 at 109-24/32, June T-bills were up seven bps at 94.94, March Eurodollars were up three basis points at 94.47 and June Eurodollars were six bps higher at 94.36.
